chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two brothers who are owned slaves, whether they are separated from each other, and about the woman and her child? He (peace be upon him) said: No, it is prohibited, except if they want that.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to separate enslaved family members in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the default legal principle that familial bonds among enslaved persons are preserved during ownership, rendering separation *haram* unless the individuals themselves consent. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on maintaining kinship ties (*silat al-rahim*) even within the institution of slavery, prioritizing the slaves' agency in altering their status. The hadith serves as a foundational text for discussions on manumission and family rights in classical fiqh.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about two brothers who are owned slaves, is effecting a separation between the two Permissible, and about the woman and her child?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, it is Prohibited, except if they want that’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of two slaves who are brothers; if they can be separated from each other or a woman slave, if she can be separated from her children. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not lawful unless they want it.’”
